[Thinking]
**Fixing errors**

I'm going through some text to make corrections: changing "of the" is necessary. I'll fix typos like "uise" to "use," "iwth" to "with," "existince" to "existence," and "clasical" to "classical." 

I’m wondering about "inhten," which probably should be "in the upper half-plane." I want to maintain the original style while clarifying "proovehten" to "prove the." Also, for the different spacing in "$U(1, 1)$" versus "$U(1,1)$," I need to keep the original style. Lastly, "the generating series" might need to be revisited for consistency.**Correcting phrasing and spellings**

I'm reviewing common phrasing and think using "the" in "a precise pullback formula of the generating series of arithmetic divisors" feels safer.

For "non-vanishing of classical theta series at any given point in the upper half-plane," I'll fix only the spelling, keeping the hyphen in "non-vanishing." The term "theta series" looks good.

BHKRY is fine as is! I'm also considering changing "embed a $U(1, 1)$ Shimura curve to many" to "into many," but it's grammar, so I'll leave it. I'm set to produce the corrected text with minimal changes!
[/Thinking]

This paper is a complement of the modularity result of Bruinier, Howard, Kudla, Rapoport and Yang (BHKRY) for the special case $U(1,1)$ not considered there. The main idea is to embed a $U(1, 1)$ Shimura curve to many $U(n-1, 1)$ Shimura varieties for big $n$, and prove a precise pullback formula of the generating series of arithmetic divisors. Afterwards, we use the modularity result of BHKRY together with the existence of non-vanishing of classical theta series at any given point in the upper half plane to prove the modularity result on $U(1, 1)$ Shimura curves.
